statement: Aramaic script derives from Phoenician, c. 8th century BCE — well established and uncontested. Aramaic's downstream branching is broad: Nabataean (a cursive regional variant) leads to Arabic script (from c. 4th century CE); Aramaic square script leads to the modern Hebrew alphabet (replacing the older Paleo-Hebrew/Phoenician-descended script); also ancestral to Syriac and, via Sogdian/Uyghur intermediaries, Mongolian script.

sources.citation: General epigraphic literature on Aramaic's Phoenician derivation and downstream branching (Nabataean/Arabic, square-script Hebrew, Syriac, Sogdian/Mongolian).
